source.snippet: Been doing hardcode agent driven coding for the past year. I feel like I now have to test all my code locally with agents reviewing them and ideally testing them. Unfortunately I feel like the traditional CI/CD testing is starting to feel like a formality. Would love to know what everyone is doing, and if I'm not the only one making a mistake. (7 points, 7 comments, Aug 2026)

problem_statement: Developers using AI coding agents find that traditional CI/CD pipelines no longer fit their workflow — tests feel like a formality, and there is no established toolchain for agent-driven code review, local agent testing, and deployment that replaces or augments existing CI/CD.
target_segment: Software developers and engineering teams at companies adopting AI-agent-driven coding workflows
notes: Active HN thread (7 pts, 7 comments, very recent Aug 2026) showing real practitioner confusion about adapting CI/CD to agent workflows. Work/professional context strong — these are employed engineers. Existing CI/CD tooling is a paid category (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, etc.), so there is clear precedent for buyers paying for this layer. Opportunity: agent-aware CI/CD orchestration or testing layer that integrates with LLM coding agents.
